# MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 Calibration checks - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
- This document describes calibration check activities for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) used in the heat treatment cell on line P3-L4.
- Applies to routine calibration verification performed after maintenance, before production cycles, and whenever accuracy concerns are raised.
- The maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 1720 mm. Use this value when verifying travel limits, detector positioning, and setup envelopes.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05 for related operational and safety procedures.

Background and intent
- The radial ring rolling mill is used to manipulate and position ring blanks for heat treatment. Calibration checks ensure that positional feedback, travel limits, and sensing systems match physical reality and the control system model.
- This procedure focuses on verification rather than full calibration. Full calibration actions that change sensor scaling or controller parameters must be performed and documented in accordance with the relevant SOPs and change control.
- The objective is to detect drift, sensor misalignment, and mechanical freeplay before these issues impact part quality or cause equipment damage.

Tools
- Portable position indicator or dimensional reference compatible with machine axes and capable of matching the maximum ring size envelope.
- Dial or electronic gauge suitable for measuring alignment references at interfaces.
- Reference ring fixture sized to envelope margins; must be compatible with the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01).
- Inspection mirror and light for access to sensor mounting points.
- Lubricant supply with part number CFW-LUB-315 for any lubrication verification steps. Do not substitute part numbers.
- Calibration log form and defect report template per document control.

Procedure
- Preparatory checks
  - Confirm machine is in a safe, de-energized access state following SOP-P3-L4-02. Lockout/tagout must be verified before accessing mechanical or sensing elements.
  - Review the last recorded calibration check entries and any outstanding defects. Identify any recurring items and note them on the calibration log.

- Mechanical envelope verification
  - Install the reference ring fixture sized to the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) to validate clearance and travel limits.
  - Move machine axes slowly by manual jog function to approach the envelope boundaries. Observe for interference, unexpected contact, or abnormal noises. Use the portable position indicator to verify actual travel endpoints correspond to controller readouts.
  - Rationale: Physical interference can cause latent offset in sensing and damage to parts. Verifying with a reference ring ensures the machine will not overtravel parts beyond the intended envelope.

- Sensor and limit switch inspection
  - Visually inspect sensor mounts for looseness, abrasion, or misalignment. Use the inspection mirror and light for hard-to-see areas.
  - Apply the electronic or dial gauge at sensor reference points and compare to controller feedback. If the sensor output deviates from the physical reading, document the delta and tag for follow-up calibration or repair.
  - Rationale: Sensors can shift due to vibration or mechanical impact. Early detection prevents drift in control loops.

- Alignment and squareness checks
  - Using the dial or electronic gauge, check alignment of key bearing housings and guide surfaces against the machine datum. Record readings on the calibration log.
  - If misalignment is detected, record severity and suspected cause. Minor adjustments may be permitted in accordance with mechanical maintenance protocols; major interventions require coordination with engineering.
  - Rationale: Proper alignment preserves tool life and maintains predictable kinematics for ring handling.

- Verification of lubrication points
  - Inspect lubrication distribution at grease fittings and contact surfaces. Confirm lubricant stock and that lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315 is in use where required.
  - Note any dry bearings or contamination and schedule corrective lubrication actions per maintenance rules.
  - Rationale: Correct lubricant specification and application prevent premature wear and sensor errors caused by mechanical looseness.

- Control system feedback check
  - With the machine powered in a controlled mode, command slow, incremental movements and compare controller-reported positions to the portable position indicator.
  - Document any discrepancies and the axis or sensor involved. If the discrepancy exceeds acceptable limits, escalate to calibration adjustment per SOP-P3-L4-03.
  - Rationale: Ensures that control system readings reflect true machine position and that operator setpoints will result in expected part motion.

Examples and expected observations
- Example: If the controller reports a travel limit at a position that physically contacts the reference ring fixture before the indicator reaches the expected value, this indicates sensor scaling or offset error. Document the discrepancy and annotate the calibration log.
- Example: If lens housings or proximity switches show a shift from their documented mounting positions, note the movement and the suspected origin such as mechanical impact or inadequate clamp torque. Follow SOP-P3-L4-05 for repair authorization.

Acceptance criteria
- All mechanical travel limits must allow clearance for the reference ring sized at the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) without unintended contact.
- Sensor position feedback must match physical measurements within the tolerances defined in the active calibration standard. Any exception must be entered into the calibration log and escalated.
- Lubrication points must be serviced with lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315 where specified. Any deviation from this part number is not acceptable.
- Any corrective actions that alter sensor scaling or mechanical datum must be recorded and tracked via the change control process and referenced in the calibration log.

Records to keep
- The calibration log must capture date, technician name, items inspected, measurement results, discrepancies observed, corrective actions taken, and references to SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05 as applicable.
- Defect reports for items outside acceptance criteria must be filed and routed per maintenance workflow. Attach photographic evidence where practical.
- Retain all records in the document control system and reference them during subsequent calibration checks.

Notes and escalation
- If uncertainty exists about the acceptability of any measurement or finding, consult engineering and reference SOP-P3-L4-03 before making adjustments that affect production parameters.
- Do not proceed with production use of the machine until all critical discrepancies affecting safety or part integrity are resolved and documented.
